title: Donut in 5 steps (demo)
goal: Make a brown donut in Blender with the simplest possible path: delete the cube, add a torus, give it a brown material and show it in Material Preview

milestones.goal: Delete the default cube (keep the camera and the light)
milestones.done_when: The outliner (top right) no longer lists 'Cube'; 'Camera' and 'Light' may still be there
hints: Simplest path: the Cube is already selected in a new scene (orange outline). Move the pointer over the 3D viewport, press X, then click Delete
If the Cube is not selected: click the cube once in the viewport first, then press X and click Delete
Do not press A (select all) and do not delete the Camera or the Light
Do not use the Edit menu, the outliner right-click menu or any other path
milestones.teach: Every new Blender scene starts with a cube. We remove it to make room for the donut.

milestones.goal: Add a torus with its default settings
milestones.done_when: A ring-shaped object is in the middle of the viewport and the outliner lists 'Torus'
hints: Simplest path: click the 'Add' menu in the header at the top left of the 3D viewport, hover 'Mesh', then click 'Torus'
Keep every default value: do not open or change the 'Add Torus' panel that appears at the bottom left
Do not use Shift+A, the search, or the Edit Mode; stay in Object Mode
If the torus is small, that is fine: do not scale, move or zoom
milestones.teach: A torus is a ready-made ring: the perfect starting shape for a donut.

milestones.goal: Give the torus a new material
milestones.done_when: In the Properties editor, the Material tab shows a material named 'Material' (or 'Material.001') with 'Surface: Principled BSDF'
hints: The torus is already selected right after you add it; if not, click it once in the viewport
Simplest path: in the Properties editor on the right, click the red sphere icon (Material Properties), near the bottom of the vertical tab column
Click the big 'New' button. Nothing else
Do not open the Shading workspace or the node editor
milestones.teach: A material describes how a surface looks: its color, how shiny it is, how it reflects light.

milestones.goal: Set the material's Base Color to golden brown (hex C68642)
milestones.done_when: The Base Color swatch in the Material tab is brown (warm orange-brown), not white or grey
hints: Simplest path: in the Material tab, click the white swatch next to 'Base Color' to open the color picker
Click the 'Hex' field in the picker, select its text, type C68642 and press Enter
Do not drag in the color wheel and do not change Metallic, Roughness or any other value
Click anywhere outside the picker to close it
milestones.teach: Base Color is the surface's own color, before light and reflections. Typing the hex value is the most precise way to set it.

milestones.goal: Show the donut in Material Preview to see its color
milestones.done_when: The viewport shading is Material Preview (the third of the four sphere buttons at the top right of the viewport is highlighted) and the donut looks brown
hints: Simplest path: at the top right of the 3D viewport there are four small sphere buttons; click the third one (Material Preview)
Do not use the Z pie menu and do not switch to Rendered (the fourth button), which is slower
The first preview can take a few seconds to compile shaders: wait, do not click again
milestones.teach: Solid mode shows shapes in grey; Material Preview shows the real colors of your materials.
